points.name: sports.settings.switch.register
points.interpretation: Two layout paths register C5BEFC8 on the setting row or inner element. User data is a pointer to the setting record.

points.name: sports.settings.switch.event_data
points.interpretation: C5BEFC8 forwards the user-data record to the reminder setting row builder.

points.name: sports.settings.picker.confirm_register
points.interpretation: Two picker layout branches register C5BC940, which validates event and saves the chosen setting.

points.name: sports.settings.picker.confirm_register_alt
points.interpretation: Two additional picker layout branches register the same confirmation callback.

points.name: sports.settings.picker.event_data
points.interpretation: The confirmation callback reads a setting-record pointer, dereferences the record and writes selected values.

points.name: sports.settings.picker.change_register
points.interpretation: A picker branch registers C5BD3E0 with filter 0 for picker interaction state.

points.name: sports.settings.picker.focus_register
points.interpretation: A picker branch registers C5BC830 with filter 9.

points.name: sports.settings.picker.value_register
points.interpretation: A picker branch registers C5BD060 with filter 11 to refresh associated picker state.

points.name: sports.settings.radio.runway_register
points.interpretation: Type 36 branch registers runway confirmation callback C5C1984, which writes several sport settings.

points.name: sports.settings.radio.runway_data
points.interpretation: Runway confirmation reads and dereferences a setting-record pointer before writing configuration.

evidence: The sports manifest registers the five descriptors. Each create stores a private allocation at descriptor +60; each destroy clears it. The switch row callback retrieves its data and rebuilds setting rows. The picker confirmation callback reads a record pointer, derives a value from picker state and invokes setting-save functions. The type-36 radio button callback reads the same kind of event data, saves multiple settings and emits notifications.
scope: Specific shared LVGL registration and user-data calls only; no claim to intercept all ways of modifying sport settings. Picker registration pairs cover four distinct static call sites and the three other picker callbacks belong to one branch.
limitations: User-data results are pointers to records, not booleans; replacing them with invalid or mismatched pointers can crash or corrupt settings. Skipping callbacks or page destruction can leave configuration, timers or resources inconsistent. The slots do not provide a thread barrier. Device behavior and rollback remain unverified.
